 About the client 
 Our client is is an international manufacturer of analytical instruments, with a Research & Development centre in Cluj-Napoca and a manufacturing facility in Nușfalău. As part of a group-level initiative, the company is strengthening cybersecurity across both locations and is looking for a specialist to drive this work locally, working alongside the global IT team.
 About the role 
 A cybersecurity framework has already been defined with the support of external consultants. Your job is to turn it into working security controls. You will own the local implementation, starting with the R&D environment in Cluj (Phase 1) and continuing with the manufacturing site in Nușfalău (Phase 2).
 This is a hands-on, implementation-oriented role, not a SOC monitoring or purely audit position. You will work closely with internal and external IT teams, R&D staff and production stakeholders, making sure security standards are adopted in practice, not just documented.
 Responsibilities: 
Lead the local implementation of the Cybersecurity Framework, first in R&D (Cluj), then in manufacturing (Nușfalău)
Support the R&D team in implementing the cybersecurity requirements of the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)
Review the current security setup, identify weaknesses and build a prioritised plan to address key risks
Establish and maintain baseline security standards for computers, servers, networks, cloud services and user accounts
Review user access and administrator permissions to ensure appropriate, role-based access
Improve protection through secure configurations, patching, endpoint protection, firewalls and secure remote access
Work with IT teams to make sure backups are protected and critical systems and data can be restored
Review security alerts, investigate suspicious activity and help coordinate incident response
Create and maintain clear procedures for incident handling and recovery from disruptions
Support NIS2 preparations by implementing agreed security measures and documenting completed work
Provide technical information and documentation to external legal counsel, who will assess NIS2 applicability
Drive change in uptime-critical environments such as production, building support for new security requirements
Raise employee awareness of common risks such as phishing, unsafe downloads and weak passwords
Report clearly to management on security risks, completed improvements and open items
 Qualifications: 
At least 5 years of experience in cybersecurity or IT security
Solid IT infrastructure background: networks, servers, endpoints, identity and cloud services
Practical experience assessing security risks and implementing improvements, not only recommending them
Ability to work independently, set priorities and own a project from planning to delivery
Strong stakeholder management skills, including bringing reluctant teams along with change
Ability to explain technical topics in plain language to both technical and non-technical audiences
Fluent English, spoken and written
Experience with Microsoft 365, Intune, Fortinet, Bitdefender or similar tools is a plus
Experience with vulnerability management, security monitoring or frameworks such as NIS2, ISO 27001, NIST or CIS is a plus
Experience with security work in manufacturing or R&D environments is an advantage, but not required
